summary: Recent election results are generating renewed momentum for D.C. statehood advocacy, with supporters pointing to midterm outcomes as creating new opportunities for the cause. Advocates continue to emphasize that the District's population already exceeds that of some existing states, and they have documented recent instances in which they say Congress has acted against D.C.'s local authority. Without statehood, D.C. residents have no senators, and their one delegate to the House cannot vote on the House floor.
